AE.name: United Arab Emirates
AE.source: Federal Law No. 2 of 1971 as amended by Federal Decree-Law No. 13 of 2019, as the UAE Government's flag guidebook states it: the flag's width is twice its height

AR.name: Argentina
AR.source: Decreto 1650/2010 (Boletín Oficial 2010-11-23) sets the flag's measures through IRAM standards DEF D 7679:2002, DEF D 7677:2002, DEF D 7675:2003 and DEF D 7674:2004. Its own text, Ley 23.208 and the government's flag page give no proportions
AR.note: The IRAM standards are not free to read, so the ratio stays open. The shipped 8:5 is what Commons draws.

AT.name: Austria
AT.source: Bundes-Verfassungsgesetz Art. 8a gives the colours and three equal bands, no ratio. The Wappengesetz (BGBl. 159/1984) gives 2:3 for the federal service flag only
AT.note: No official ratio found for the national flag.

AU.name: Australia
AU.source: Flags Act 1953 (Cth), Schedule 1 and the drawing in the Second Schedule: every measure is a fraction of the flag's width. The Prime Minister and Cabinet booklet 'Australian Flags' labels the length 2X and the hoist X
AU.note: The Schedule's words do not state the length; the ratio is the drawing's and the booklet's.

BD.name: Bangladesh
BD.source: Bangladesh National Anthem, Flag and Emblem Order, 1972 (President's Order 130 of 1972), Second Schedule: when the length is 10 feet the width is 6 feet

BE.name: Belgium
BE.source: No law or government page giving the ratio was found; the shipped drawing is 15:13

BR.name: Brazil
BR.source: Lei 5.700 of 1971, art. 5: the width is divided into 14 modules and the length is 20 modules

CA.name: Canada
CA.source: Canadian Heritage, Description of the National Flag of Canada: twice as long as it is wide (proportion 2:1, 64 units by 32)

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.source: Federal Act on the Protection of the Swiss Coat of Arms and Other Public Signs (SR 232.21), art. 3 and Annex 2: a Swiss cross on a square field

CN.name: China
CN.source: Law on the National Flag (1990, revised 2020), annex 国旗制法说明 (Kokki seihō setsumei / Description of how the flag is made), item 1: the length and the height are as three to two
CN.note: A copy of the law's text on 12371.cn.

CO.name: Colombia
CO.source: Ley 12 of 1984, art. 1, gives the three bands (yellow half, blue and red a quarter each) and no ratio; the merchant flag is 3 metres by 2 under Decreto 309 of 1980
CO.note: No official ratio found for the national flag.

CZ.name: Czechia
CZ.source: Act No. 3/1993 Coll. on the State Symbols, § 4(1): the ratio of the flag's width to its length is 2:3

DE.name: Germany
DE.source: Anordnung über die deutschen Flaggen of 1996, I.1: the ratio of the height to the length of the cloth is 3 to 5

DK.name: Denmark
DK.source: Lov om flagning (LOV 1449 of 2024-12-10), explanatory notes: the cross is 1/7 of the height, the fields at the hoist are squares and the outer fields are 1 3/4 times the inner ones, which is 28:37
DK.note: 28:37 is worked out from those fractions; the law does not write it.

EG.name: Egypt
EG.source: No law or government page giving the ratio was found; the shipped drawing is 3:2

ES.name: Spain
ES.source: Real Decreto 1511/1977 (Reglamento de Banderas, Estandartes, Guiones, Insignias y Distintivos): in the normal proportion the length is three halves of the width
ES.note: Ley 39/1981 and the Constitution (art. 4) give the bands and no ratio. Whether the Reglamento is still in force in full was not checked.

FI.name: Finland
FI.source: Laki Suomen lipusta 380/1978 on finlex.fi should give 11:18; its text could not be read from here (the page needs a script)

FR.name: France
FR.source: Constitution, art. 2: the national emblem is the tricolour flag, blue, white, red. It gives no ratio, and a search of Légifrance found no decree that does
FR.note: No official ratio found; the search was not exhaustive.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.source: No Act fixes the Union Flag's proportions. The Flag Institute (not a government body) specifies 3:5 on land and 1:2 at sea
GB.note: No official ratio found; the shipped 5:3 is the Flag Institute's land flag.

GR.name: Greece
GR.source: Law 851/1978 (FEK 233 A) regulates the national flag; its text could not be read from here

ID.name: Indonesia
ID.source: Undang-Undang No. 24 of 2009, art. 4: the flag is a rectangle whose width is two thirds of its length

IL.name: Israel
IL.source: Israel State Archives, The Flag and the Emblem: the official measurements are 160 by 220 cm (the Flag and Emblem Law, 5709-1949)

IN.name: India
IN.source: Flag Code of India 2002, as the Press Information Bureau's FAQ states it: the ratio of the length to the height (width) is 3:2

IR.name: Iran
IR.source: Constitution, art. 18, gives the colours, the emblem and the motto and no ratio; a law or regulation that does was not found

IT.name: Italy
IT.source: Presidency of the Council of Ministers, State Ceremonial Office: the proportions are fixed (height 2/3 of the length). The Constitution, art. 12, gives three equal vertical bands and no ratio

JP.name: Japan
JP.source: 国旗及び国歌に関する法律 (Kokki oyobi kokka ni kansuru hōritsu / Act on the National Flag and Anthem, Act No. 127 of 1999), Annex 1: the height is two thirds of the length

KP.name: North Korea
KP.source: Socialist Constitution, art. 170: the ratio of the width to the length is 1:2

KR.name: South Korea
KR.source: National Archives of Korea, how the flag is made: the length (across) and the width (down) of the flag are 3:2 except in special cases
KR.note: The page does not name the Enforcement Decree of the National Flag Act; the decree's text was not read.

KZ.name: Kazakhstan
KZ.source: Office of the President, National Flag of Kazakhstan: the ratio of the flag's width to its length is 1:2 (Constitutional Law on the State Symbols, 2007)

LU.name: Luxembourg
LU.source: Loi du 23 juin 1972 sur les emblèmes nationaux, art. 3: proportions of 5 to 3 or of 2 to 1
LU.note: The law allows two shapes; 5:3 is the one shipped.

MX.name: Mexico
MX.source: Ley sobre el Escudo, la Bandera y el Himno Nacionales, art. 3: the proportion of the flag's width to its length is four to seven

NG.name: Nigeria
NG.source: No law or government page giving the ratio was found; the shipped drawing is 2:1

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.source: The government's flag instruction (the Rijksvlaginstructie) is where a ratio would be; it could not be read from here, and the Royal Decree of 1937 was not found to give one

NO.name: Norway
NO.source: Lov om Norges Flag (flaggloven) of 1898, § 1: the width is to the length as 16 to 22

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.source: Ministry for Culture and Heritage, New Zealand flag: the flag can be any size, with the length always twice the width. The Flags, Emblems, and Names Protection Act 1981, s 10(c), lets the Minister set the standard proportions

OM.name: Oman
OM.source: Royal Decree 99/2026 (Official Gazette 1672, 2026-11-01), Annex 1, Second: the official measurements are the sheet of 350 cm by 200 cm, a red vertical unit of 116.67 cm and three horizontal bands of 66.67 cm
OM.note: The sheet is an image. A copy of the decree on qanoon.om; the Gazette itself was not found online.

PH.name: Philippines
PH.source: Republic Act No. 8491 (Flag and Heraldic Code of the Philippines, 1998), sec. 27: width 1, length 2

PK.name: Pakistan
PK.source: Cabinet Division, National Flag of the Federation of Pakistan: the resolution of the Constituent Assembly of 1947-08-11 gives a rectangle in the proportion of length to width 3:2
PK.note: The page is a scan; the ratio comes from a search result quoting the resolution.

PL.name: Poland
PL.source: Ustawa z dnia 31 stycznia 1980 r. o godle, barwach i hymnie Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej oraz o pieczęciach państwowych, annex (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 299): the ratio of the flag's width to its length is 5:8

PT.name: Portugal
PT.source: Presidency of the Republic, Bandeira Nacional: the height is two thirds of the length (Decree of 1911-06-19 and the technical opinion in Diário do Governo no. 150 of 1911-06-30)

RU.name: Russia
RU.source: Federal Constitutional Law No. 1-FKZ of 2000-12-25, art. 1: the ratio of the flag's width to its length is 2:3

SA.name: Saudi Arabia
SA.source: The flag regulation of 1393 AH (1973) makes the width two thirds of the length, as the Saudi Press Agency states it
SA.note: The regulation's own text was not found online.

SE.name: Sweden
SE.source: Lag (1982:269) om Sveriges flagga, 2 §: the height of the rectangular flag is to its length as 10 to 16

TG.name: Togo
TG.source: The Constitution of the Fourth Republic, art. 3, gives five stripes and the red square with its star and no ratio; the Constitution of 2024 leaves the national emblem to law
TG.note: No official ratio found. The shipped 3:2 is the Commons file's own; sources elsewhere disagree (1:1.618, 3:5, 2:3).

TH.name: Thailand
TH.source: Government of Thailand, Flag: the flag is rectangular, 6 parts wide and 9 parts long (Flag Act B.E. 2522)

TR.name: Türkiye
TR.source: Türk Bayrağı Kanunu 2893, art. 2, takes the flag's shape and proportions from a table annexed to the law; the table could not be read from here

UA.name: Ukraine
UA.source: Constitution, art. 20, gives two equal bands, blue over yellow, and no ratio; a law that does was not found

US.name: United States
US.source: Executive Order 10834 of 1959-08-21, sec. 21: the standard sizes are in the ratio 1:1.9 (hoist 10.00 feet, fly 19.00 feet; 20.00 by 38.00)
US.note: Sec. 3 refers to an attached drawing of the proportions, which the page does not show.

VN.name: Vietnam
VN.source: Constitution of 2013, art. 13: the flag is a rectangle whose width is two thirds of its length

ZA.name: South Africa
ZA.source: Constitution of 1996, Schedule 1, section 1(1): the flag is rectangular and one and a half times longer than it is wide
